title: Semantically-aware prefix proxy cache and staleness fallback for embeddings endpoint
creator: Amina Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight prefix proxy cache that performs semantically-aware normalization and signature lookup before forwarding requests to the main embeddings service. Aim is to reduce end-to-end latency for high-volume prefix-heavy workloads (autocomplete, rerank pipelines) and reduce duplicate embedding compute across tenants while providing a controlled staleness fallback when cached vectors are slightly outdated.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy cache returns cached embedding within 8ms P50 for cached prefixes on dedicated capacity instances
Cache hit rate >= 35% for customer test corpus (search and rerank traces) after warmup
End-to-end P99 latency for embeddings endpoint improves by >= 12% for target workloads without increasing error rate
Fallback path gracefully serves cold embeddings when signature mismatch or expired, with clear metrics and no request-level failures
No customer data cross-tenant leakage: cache keys are isolated by tenant and model-version tags
design_notes: Proxy sits in front of embeddings generator as a thin stateless service with a local hot-LRU and backing shared distributed store (Redis cluster) for warm prefixes
Normalization pipeline: trim, unicode normalize (NFKC), collapse whitespace, punctuation pruning for short prefixes, and token-aware case folding to reduce superficial variance
Signature algorithm: shingled MinHash (k=6) + 64-bit reservoir hash to capture near-duplicates while remaining computationally cheap; store signature + short content fingerprint
Eviction policy: tiered TTLs (hot short TTL 30m, warm 6h, cold 72h) with adaptive extension for frequently accessed keys and explicit invalidation on model rollout
Staleness fallback: if signature similarity >= 0.85 and embedding age <= warm_ttl + 30m, serve cached vector with metadata header 'X-Cache-Stale: true' and async recompute to refresh cache
Privacy: cache stores only embeddings and truncated fingerprints, never raw text beyond the minimal normalized prefix used for signature computation
Observability: tag metrics by tenant, model, signature-cohort, and prefix-length bucket; emit cache hit/miss, skirted-stale-serving events, recompute queue length
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): implement normalization + signature lib in Rust for perf; benchmark on historical traces (1 week) - owner: Diego
Phase 2: proxy service skeleton in Go with local LRU layer and Redis backing; include tenant isolation and key construction - owner: Eng Infra
Phase 3: implement staleness heuristics + async refresh queue (Kafka) and integrate with existing embeddings generator via gRPC - owner: Model Serving team
Phase 4: end-to-end tests with synthetic high-prefix workload and internal rerank traces; measure metrics and tune thresholds - owner: SRE + Eng QA
Phase 5: staged rollout (see rollout plan) and post-roll metrics review; if regressions observed, automatic disable-by-tenant flag available
testing_plan: Unit tests: normalization edge cases (unicode, emojis, punctuation), signature collisions
Integration: proxy -> redis -> embeddings generator local cluster test harness
Load test: replay anonymized production prefix traces to validate hit rates and latency under 80th/95th percentile QPS
A/B test: enable for 10% of hostnames with detailed telemetry, compare latency/cost against control
Regression: ensure accuracy of reranker (downstream) by running end-to-end relevance evals pre/post rollout; delta in nDCG must be <= 0.01
rollout_plan: Canary 1: internal tenants only at 1% traffic for 48 hours; verify cache correctness and hit/miss metrics
Canary 2: select customers (opt-in) at 10% traffic for 72 hours; check downstream rerank metrics and cost impact
Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 10 days with automated abort thresholds for increased p99 latency or drop in relevance beyond allowance
Rollback: feature flag to disable proxy per-region and per-tenant; fallback to direct embeddings generator path
Post-launch: 30-day observation window with weekly review and final decision to promote to Dedicated default
metrics: Cache hit rate (tenant/model signature cohort) - target >= 0.35
Embeddings endpoint P50/P95/P99 latency - target P99 improvement >= 12% for covered traffic
Compute savings (GPU-minutes) attributable to cache - report daily
Stale-serve rate (requests served with X-Cache-Stale) - should be < 5% of hits
Async recompute backlog length - must remain < 5000 per region under steady state
Accuracy delta: nDCG and rerank precision on canary data - delta <= 0.01
risks: Signature collisions leading to incorrect reuse of embedding for different content; mitigated by two-tier check (signature + short fingerprint) and conservative similarity thresholds
Serving stale embeddings that degrade rerank quality; mitigated by staleness headers, async refresh, and conservative age windows for stale-serving
Cross-tenant leakage via misconstructed keys; mitigation: explicit tenant-scoped keys and unit tests to validate isolation
Operational complexity and extra moving parts (proxy, redis, queue) increasing failure modes; mitigation: lightweight proxy design and default disable flag
Cost of additional Redis storage and recompute traffic may offset savings for low-reuse workloads; we'll gate on observed hit rate before global rollout
